<!-- felucca-firmware-watch:v1 -->
Review each source commit for a justified bug fix, optimization, feature adaptation or backport in `kmplngj/Felucca`. Create actionable GitHub issues only when current Felucca evidence supports them; link existing issues instead of duplicating work. This issue stores durable progress for a daily 09:00 Europe/Berlin scheduled review.

## Scope and initial coverage

The user requested all discussed FM-1 firmwares and the additional Schwung/module/Nibbi references, plus a gradual review of their complete older history. There are **20 repositories / 22 branches**, including Melodee `next` and GHOULBOX `research/flash-savings`. Branches are tracked explicitly; new or renamed branches require a visible scope update.

All initial snapshots were verified against GitHub and complete Git commit graphs on 2026-10-12. The initial historical queue has **4,747 distinct repository/SHA pairs**; **138 newer pairs** are reachable beyond the documented review snapshots. Counts deduplicate branches within a repository, and may contain shared commits across repositories. The dated reviews are useful source assessments, **not evidence that those historical commits were individually reviewed**. No historical coverage is credited merely because a snapshot was reviewed.

### Pending-source initialization policy

New sources added while a run holds a frozen live-tip/cache inventory are stored in the machine-readable `pending_source_additions` array. This is durable source registration, not a journal assessment. Preserve this array during checkpoint updates. At the **start of the next audit run**, before freezing inventory or selecting commits, initialize each pending source: verify repository ID/branch and pinned SHA, create/fetch its complete Git DAG cache, collect fresh branch tips, retain the immutable historical target, and append its entry to `repositories`. Remove only the successfully initialized pending entry and recalculate catalog/queue totals from full DAGs and the journal. Do not credit snapshot coverage or alter previous journals/frontiers. Missing sources/SHAs remain pending with an explicit blocker; independent sources can continue. This avoids changing an active run's assumptions and keeps requested sources recoverable.

## Durable progress and recovery

The JSON below is the configuration and checkpoint cache. The authoritative record of reviewed commits is the append-only journal in this issue's comments. Each comment carries `<!-- felucca-firmware-watch-journal:v1 -->` and a JSON `records` array. A record includes repository, full source SHA, parents, branch membership, recent/history queue, commit title, changed paths, Felucca comparison SHA, disposition, rationale, source/native evidence and linked issue URLs. Dispositions are `bug`, `optimization`, `feature`, `backport`, `already_present`, `existing_issue`, `not_applicable`, `needs_input` or `pending`. The last two are nonterminal records and never count as reviewed coverage. An incomplete assessment is pending and is never journaled as reviewed.

Each repository/SHA is assessed once. Reuse a completed result when that SHA is also reachable from another tracked branch. Equivalent changes across different repositories may reuse evidence only after checking that the patch and native applicability match, and still receive their own explicit record.

For recent work, `recent_frontiers` starts at the documented snapshots only to split old/new queues; these initial boundary hashes do **not** claim reviewed coverage. Freeze `pinned_recent_targets` during an incomplete batch. Enumerate the complete DAG in oldest-first topological order, with all tracked target tips included and all frontier ancestors excluded. Advance each frontier only when every reachable commit in its interval has a completed journal record. Once that frozen interval is complete (including an empty interval), pin the newly fetched branch tips for the next interval. needs_input and pending records never count as reviewed coverage.

The historical queue is every commit reachable from the immutable `historical_targets`, including roots and merges. Enumerate it oldest-first in topological order and subtract confirmed journal records. Never use dates, first-parent-only logs, API page limits or the last displayed SHA as proof of contiguous coverage.

For each completed assessment: create/reuse the actionable issue first, read back its URL, append and read back the journal record, then refresh this body's summary/checkpoints. If interrupted after issue creation, recover the existing issue by its stable marker. If interrupted after journaling, rebuild the cached progress from all paginated journal comments. Never skip a commit because a checkpoint write failed.

Candidate issues and evidence comments use `<!-- felucca-upstream:<repository>@<full-sha>:<stable-topic> -->` markers. Inspect all open/closed issues and comments, not search indexing alone, before a retry. Record the decision even when no issue is justified.

Local setup/cache files under ignored `build/firmware-watch-setup/` are disposable; this GitHub issue is the durable state. Clone/fetch caches and temporary analysis remain under ignored `build/`. Do not modify the shared firmware working tree. Serial runs use an atomic local lease under `/Users/jankampling/.codex/automation-state/felucca-firmware-watch/`, with a random run ID, a two-hour expiry and explicit release.

## Review policy

Read actual diffs and necessary callers/tests; commit messages and upstream performance claims alone are insufficient. Check current Felucca implementation, prior review documents, existing tickets, licensing and JieLi Clang 4.0.1 constraints. A bug issue requires evidence that the problematic behavior is present here. An optimization candidate needs a bounded baseline/A-B measurement plan, arithmetic/sound invariants and all relevant flash/RAM/NOINIT/CPU deadlines. A feature/backport needs a native integration design, stable IDs, serializer/protocol compatibility, acceptance criteria and applicable hardware gates.

Evaluate tools, tests and platform work as well as DSP. Inspect merge resolution differences as well as all merged commits. Source generated from an earlier commit must not silently count that earlier source commit as reviewed. Documentation-only, generated publishing and irrelevant platform changes still receive a reasoned decision.

Review queues round-robin across repositories with recent commits first and a reserved historical share, so active sources and the 3,230-commit Schwung history cannot starve the other sources. Bound each run to at most 60 minutes or 50 assessments, allocating roughly 60% to recent work and 40% to history when both exist. Persist after every assessment and stop with exact pending work when a limit or missing input is reached.

History rewrites, removed branches, unavailable commits, authentication and incomplete/paginated diffs are visible blockers. Retain old checkpoints; continue independent sources. Do not silently rebase/reset cursors. Firmware implementation, baseline regeneration, flashing, publishing, merging or unrelated repository writes are outside this task.

## Setup validation

One SLOOP publishing commit has a confirmed journal record. Its three preceding recent commits remain pending, so the frontier has not advanced. Historical coverage remains zero; the initial newer queue now has 137 unreviewed commits. Complete Git DAG enumeration, snapshot ancestry and journal read-back were checked.

The old-only commit remains in the original historical queue. No journal decision was transferred or modified; **102 records / 101 completed repository/SHA pairs** remain unchanged. At admission, source work was **38 historical / 7 recent**, with all seven new SHAs unreviewed. The subsequent individual audit below completed those seven recent assessments; the historical queue remains open.

A confirmed comment with `<!-- felucca-firmware-watch-reconciliation:v1 -->` and a JSON `reconciliations` array is the authoritative rewrite intake record; `history_reconciliations` is its cache. Replay this record after an interrupted cache update, checking source identity, archived original checkpoints and complete DAGs. For this explicitly accepted interval, enumerate the complete reachable frozen target **minus reachable retained frontier**, oldest topological order, then subtract exact repository/full-SHA terminal journal records. Non-ancestry of the retained frontier alone is no longer a blocker for this specific recorded interval. Do not skip the old-only historical commit, carry decisions to new SHAs, or replace immutable historical targets. Advance the frontier only after all interval commits have completed records. Detect future rewrites against the **current frozen target**, preserve unreviewed intervals and old checkpoints, and obtain another explicit reconciliation before adopting a further incompatible target.

Evidence: [https://github.com/kmplngj/Felucca/issues/152#issuecomment-6149168784](https://github.com/kmplngj/Felucca/issues/152#issuecomment-6149168784). Git cache retains the old commit under a dedicated reference; caches remain disposable, with all authoritative checkpoints and decisions in this issue. Global queues were re-enumerated from the full cached DAGs and the previous audit's observed tips plus this freshly verified SMK37 tip: **5319 historical / 365 newer** remain. ### Quixotic7/ChoralRootFM1 `0b8909daa8b7` — bug

Inspected the per-part send ownership, picker key ownership, session tags and removal of forced saves during tails. Native send/picker contracts differ intentionally and are not imported. ### charlesvestal/schwung-gate `175a60a1ab30` — not_applicable

Initial ARM64 Gate/Expand plugin uses stereo peak following, hysteresis, attack/hold/release and float/log/exp arithmetic to attenuate low-level material. Native Felucca is a synthesizer without the external audio-input chain this plugin targets (#78 is prospective), and per-voice envelopes plus existing silent-bus work already own release/inactivity behavior. A master noise gate would alter intentional soft notes and FX tails, not provide a sound-preserving resource optimization. No demonstrated native noise-gating need or matching bug justifies a new issue; plugin loader/release metadata is platform-specific.
